newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Nov 26.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Tuesday:
- Duke Power Co and PanEnergy Corp are to merge in a $7.7 billion stock swap.
- Borland International Inc named a former executive of Apple Computer Inc as its chairman and chief executive officer.
- The Dow Jones industrial average passed the 6,500-point mark for the first time, closing at 6,547.79, up 76.03.
- U.S. broadcasting, consumer electronics and computer industries agreed on a technical standard for the next generation of television.
- David Kessler resigned as commissioner of the Food and Drug Administration.
- China warned Walt Disney Co that the company's role in a film about the Dalai Lama might jeopardise its plans to invest in the country's entertainment industry.
- Bank Keycorp Ltd will sell more than 100 rural branches.
- The packaged-food industry is struggling amidst a price war.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton persuaded leaders of Asian Pacific countries to try to lower tariffs on computers and other data technologies by the end of the century.
- Prices for U.S. treasury securities ended higher in a mild rally.
- The United Nations will allow Iraq to sell oil for food and other emergency supplies.
- Italy still has some way to go before it convinces other members of the European Union that it can be a part of a single currency.
- Visa accused American Express Co of trademark infringement.
- Power Computing Corp agreed to license a new computer operating system with Be Inc.
- Everen of Everen Capital insisted it was not trading ahead of its customers on the NASDAQ stock market.
- MCA Inc of Seagram Co Ltd will buy practically all of the talk shows of Multimedia Entertainment for $1.7 billion.
